findings.title: Unbounded DOCX table spans trigger multi-gigabyte renderer allocations
findings.summary: Admitted DOCX gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter values become allocation lengths without a semantic column or derived-work budget. A tiny table can exhaust the rendering process.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood document-controlled process denial of service; impact is availability of the embedding renderer, with deployment-wide impact unknown. Host memory/CPU isolation can limit the blast radius.

confidence.rationale: The complete input-to-allocation path and absence of semantic bounds were independently confirmed in current source; no dynamic exploit was run.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded allocation from untrusted table dimensions

codeEvidence.label: Renderer admission and altChunk expansion
Unbounded WML span
Unbounded row grid skips
Document-sized grid allocation
Document-sized merge tracking

rootCause.summary: Numeric table spans are parsed as usize with only a positive minimum, then summed into occupancy and used directly by vec!/resize.

findings.remediation: Enforce a maximum effective table-column count and aggregate derived-memory/work budget before any allocation. Use checked arithmetic for span sums and col+span; return a typed refusal for oversized gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter.

assertions: A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits a tiny shallow XML part yet requests a 4,000,000,000-byte f32 column vector.
gridBefore and gridAfter synthesize RawCells with the same unchecked span, and merge tracking adds another span-sized allocation.
counterEvidence: Package compressed/inflated bytes, entry count and XML depth/tag limits are enforced.
SECURITY.md recommends process resource limits; those limits constrain hosting impact but do not bound per-table derived allocations.
Markdown projection's span clamp does not control the PDF/PNG table pipeline.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; no shared-service deployment supplied.
validation.summary: Public PDF/PNG/report rendering reaches with_layout admission, collect_blocks/walk_container/table_block, then the unbounded semantic grid sinks. Admission checks bytes/depth/tags rather than WML numeric span values.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admit_package -> with_layout DOM -> table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> occupancy -> cols.resize/open.resize
dataflow.outcome: Excessive memory use or allocation abort

impact.why: Crashes or resource starvation affect the renderer process; wider deployment impact is not established.

likelihood.why: One ordinary untrusted document field directly determines large allocations under default and compare admission budgets.

reachability.summary: Reachable through Rust PDF/PNG/render/report APIs and wrappers; requires the victim to render attacker-supplied DOCX. No operator configuration control is needed.
reachability.entrypoint: docx_to_pdf_with, docx_to_png, render/report and binding/MCP render consumers

attackPath.summary: A document supplier sends a small DOCX containing a huge positive table span to any renderer consumer, causing allocation proportional to the numeric value.

remediationTests: Small admitted documents with oversized gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter must fail before allocating proportional buffers.
Verify cumulative spans exceeding the column/work budget are refused, including integer-overflow cases.
